jobs.title: Postdoctoral position in experimental particle physics with the ATLAS experiment
jobs.description:
The Department of Physics and Astronomy at Uppsala University, Sweden has an opening for a two-year postdoctoral position in experimental particle physics with the ATLAS experiment, focusing on studies of the nature of the Higgs boson, both through the creation of two Higgs bosons and two top quarks, as well as searches for signs of compositeness. Uppsala University is one of the founding members of the ATLAS experiment and the research group has many years of experience with di-Higgs searches and searches for phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

Duties
The main duties will be to take a leading role in the development of analysis methods to search for the production of two top quarks and two Higgs bosons in the HH to bbbb final state, as well as exploring synergies with searches for Higgs compositeness through the creation of vector-like quarks. In addition, the successful candidate will be expected to teach university courses, to co-supervise students and to contribute to the maintenance and operation of the ATLAS experiment, as required by the collaboration.
Administration related to teaching, supervision and research will also be necessary.

Requirements
A PhD degree in physics or a foreign degree equivalent to a PhD degree in physics. The degree needs to be obtained by the time of the decision of employment. Priority will be given to applicants who have completed their degree no more than three years before the deadline for applications. Due to special circumstances, the degree may have been obtained earlier. The three-year period can be extended due to circumstances such as sick leave, parental leave, duties in labour unions, etc.
Proficiency in written and spoken English is necessary.

Additional qualifications
Previous work with physics beyond the Standard Model and/or di-Higgs studies with the ATLAS experiment is a merit. Experience with top or Higgs to bb taggers at hadron colliders is also a merit.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position of 2 years according to central collective agreement. Full time position. Starting date 1 June 2026 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

Please see the full description and apply at https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/join-us/jobs-and-vacancies/job-details?query=915373
Only applications through the Uppsala University recruitment portal will be considered.

jobs.title: Post Doc (Consultant) for ML in natural and life sciences
jobs.description:
The Center for Scientific and High-Performance Computing (CSHPC) at Saarland University, Saarbrücken, Germany, is inviting applications for the following position commencing at the earliest opportunity.

Academic research assistant - ML Consultant

Tasks among others: Conducting independent research in applications of ML in natural and life sciences (e.g., ML-assisted molecular dynamics, protein folding, materials design, climate modeling).

Duration of employment: end of 2031 with the aim of making the position permanent, 100 % of standard working time.

Workplace/Department:

The newly established Center for Scientific and High-Performance Computing (CSHPC) will serve as a central scientific institution offering high-performance computing and related services to all departments at Saarland University and will represent the university in the German national high-performance computing initiative (NHR). The focus of this position will be on providing scientific advice and support to research groups in the NHR and at Saarland University on the efficient use and further development of cutting-edge machine learning methods on high-performance computing systems. This includes analyzing and optimizing ML workflows, evaluating and selecting suitable learning paradigms and frameworks, and developing best-practice guidelines for using scalable and reproducible ML software. The responsibilities also include close collaboration with scientific partners, organizing workshops and training courses, establishing an independent research program in the areas of ML for HPC, and contributing to the design and strategic development of Saarland University’s HPC infrastructure. 

Job requirements:

Completed university studies in computer science or a related subject area, such as mathematics or physics, preferably followed by a successful doctorate

jobs.title: Postdoctoral researcher: ATLAS Higgs Studies + FCC ALLEGRO Detector R&D
jobs.description:
Summary
The ATLAS / FCC group at the Laboratoire d’Annecy de Physique des Particules (LAPP) is inviting applications for a joint postdoctoral position for two years starting in Fall 2026. The successful candidate will be interested inmeasuring the Higgs boson self-coupling at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) with the ATLAS experiment, and in contributing to the R&D of a future detector for the Future Circular Collider electron-positron collider (FCC-ee). 

Position and Main Responsibilities
The candidate will participate in the Higgs boson pair production analysis exploiting the Run 3 LHC collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment and will contribute to the R&D of the ALLEGRO liquefied noble gas calorimeter for the future FCC-ee ALLEGRO detector, with simulation studies and hands-on work on the early prototypes of this detector. Depending on time and interest, the candidate could also contribute to feasibility studies for measurements of Higgs boson coupling properties at FCC-ee.

Thanks to the geographical proximity to CERN (50 km from LAPP), the position could be either based at LAPP with regular travel to CERN, or the other way around. Supervision of PhD and Master students could be arranged.

Required qualifications
Candidates should hold a Ph.D. degree in particle physics, obtained less than 3 years before the starting date of the position. 

Good experience in data analysis, knowledge of statistical techniques for high energy physics experiments, and an interest in detector development are required. Previous experience with the analysis of LHC data, based on solid C++ and Python expertise, is strongly appreciated. Ability to work in a large international collaboration is a must.

Fluency in English, speaking and writing (B2 minimum) is necessary. Basic knowledge of French could be useful but is not compulsory (and French courses could be provided to the candidate should they be interested).

Context
LAPP is a laboratory of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Particle Physics (IN2P3), an institute of the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS), which coordinates programs in these fields. LAPP is a joint research unit (UMR 5814) of the CNRS and the University of Savoie Mont-Blanc (USMB). More than 150 researchers, teacher-researchers, engineers, technicians, administrators, students, and foreign visitors work there. The research carried out at LAPP aims to study the physics of elementary particles and their fundamental interactions, as well as to explore their links with the great structures of the Universe. The work of the LAPP teams aims, among other things, to understand the origin of the mass of particles, to unravel the mystery of dark matter or to determine what happened to the antimatter present in our universe at the time of the Big Bang. The location of LAPP, 50 km from CERN, and the presence of the theory laboratory LAPTh in the same premises, make the LAPP campus a very attractive research place. LAPP hosts the MUST mid-range data storage and computing center.

The LAPP ATLAS group is one of the founding members of the ATLAS collaboration, and one of the key actors in the discovery of a Higgs boson and the precision measurement of its properties. The group is also involved in direct searches for new phenomena, precision measurements in gauge-boson sectors, as well as in the upgrade of the Liquid Argon calorimeter electronics and the construction of the new pixel detector for HL-LHC. The group’s expertise in physics analysis and detector development has also been directed to physics studies for the FCC-ee project and FCC detector R&D, especially in the development of the future ALLEGRO liquefied noble gas calorimeter and the measurement of the Higgs properties at FCC-ee.

Information
 Type of contract: temporary contract
Appointment period: 24 months 
Scheduled Hire date: 01/09/2026
Remuneration: starting from 3132 EUR monthly gross (including residence indemnity, about 2516 EUR monthly net)
Workplace: LAPP (Annecy 74941, France)
Attachment: ATLAS Experiment + FCC-PED
Trips: Short trips to be planned in France and abroad (collaboration meetings, conferences)
Desired level of education: PhD in particle physics
Desired work experience: maximum 3 years after PhD

How to apply
Interested candidates should apply via the CNRS Job Portal https://emploi.cnrs.fr/Offres.aspx

The candidate should provide:
  • A cover letter explaining their interest in the position;
  • A curriculum vitae including a list of key publications highlighting their personal contributions;
  • A description of research activities and interests;
The candidate should also arrange for at least 2 letters of recommendation, to be directly sent to: lapp_administration_rh_secretariat@lapp.in2p3.fr

The application and letters should be submitted by 15/5/2026 to receive full consideration.

For any enquiries about the position, please contact Marco Delmastro (marco.delmastro@cern.ch).

This position is funded by IN2P3-CNRS. CNRS is strongly committed to promoting equality and diversity. We particularly welcome applications from under-represented candidates for this post.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellowship in Experimental Particle and Strong-Field QED Physics
jobs.description:
The WIS hep-ex group is seeking an experienced postdoc to take leading a role in forefront Strong-Field QED experiments across world-leading laboratories, including SLAC (E320, US), DESY (LUXE, Germany), ELI-NP (Romania), APOLLON (France) and possibly CoReLS (Korea).

These experiments are designed to test QED at ultra intense electric fields using collisions of ~10 GeV accelerated electrons (LINAC or LWF) and ~0.01-10 PW laser pulses. The Schwinger critical field is approached and physical processes of pure non-perturbative nature may be observed.

In all experiments mentioned above, the WIS group is notably responsible for the silicon-pixel tracking detectors - the central systems for measuring the elusive non-linear Breit-Wheeler e+e- pair production in the tunneling regime, possibly for the first time. We also participate in the overall design, construction, operation and simulation of the experiments, as well as the physics-analysis. For more context on our recent work, please see NIM. A. 1083, Mar 2026, 171144 for E320, and EPJ. Spec. Top. 233, 1709–1974 (2024) for LUXE.

You will be joining amidst a surge of global experimental efforts and major funding campaigns, including a recent €14M ERC Synergy Grant (ERC-SyG) in which our lab is a key partner.

Requirements:
  • PhD and excellent knowledge in experimental particle physics,
  • Experience with detector instrumentation, preferably in the area of solid-state detectors,
  • Excellent programming skills, experience with large scale distributed computing campaigns.
Further details:
  • The post is to be based at WIS [1] with trips to SLAC, DESY, ELI-NP, APOLLON, CERN and possibly CoReLS.
  • Activities in within the ATLAS experiment at the LHC and in the DRD3 group (wide bandgap semiconductors) can also be considered, albeit with low FTE.
  • All details related to the fellowship (baseline of ~11,500 ILS/month net) are available in: https://www.weizmann.ac.il/feinberg/fellowship-aid/postdoctoral-fellows.
  • In addition to the fellowship and relocation costs, all postdocs receive an annual travel allowance of ~2k$ and the host lab covers all scientific trips if this allowance is exhausted.
  • A dedicated international office [2] operates in WIS to help researchers with ALL aspects related to the moving, working and living around WIS.
How to apply:
  • Email your CV and LOP to noam.hod@weizmann.ac.il,
  • Arrange for at least three letters to be emailed to the same address,
  • Applications are welcome from all qualified individuals
__________________________________________________________

[1] WIS is located in Rehovot, Israel, a 20 minute drive from the city of Tel Aviv. The official language (studies and administration) in WIS is English.

[2] The WIS International Office is providing a spectrum of services to our international community. The office will oversee and provide the international community non-academic and non-scientific services going forward including: Visa handling, Health insurance, Medical services, Housing and Relocating, Schools, Family and community guidance and assistance, Cultural events and activities, Hebrew Lessons and more.

[3] Postdoc applicants can start employment no later than 5 years after receiving their PhD and the employment can extend up to 7 years after receiving the PhD.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate on CMS Experiment
jobs.description:
The High Energy Physics group at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join its research program on the CMS experiment at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. The CMS group currently consists of three faculty members, a detector physicist, three postdoctoral researchers, and eight graduate students. 
     The group plays a major role in the CMS HL-LHC Inner Tracker upgrade, particularly in the production of silicon pixel detector modules for the TFPX detector. The group also holds multiple leadership roles in, and contributes broadly to, CMS operations, including computing and software operations, Tracker operations at CERN, online and offline data quality monitoring and certification, and the development of advanced machine learning techniques for CMS data processing and analysis. In physics, the group pursues measurements in Higgs, electroweak, and top-quark physics, as well as searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. 
   In addition to its CMS activities, the Nebraska HEP group participates in several astroparticle physics experiments, including the Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland (RNO-G), IceCube-Gen2, and the Askaryan Radio Array at the South Pole. 
 
The successful applicant will play a major role in the CMS HL-LHC Inner Tracker project. During the initial phase of the appointment, the postdoctoral researcher will work at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, playing a major role in the production and testing of TFPX silicon detector modules in the Nebraska HEP instrumentation laboratory. This phase is expected to extend approximately 1–1.5 years. Following completion of module production, the researcher will relocate to CERN, to contribute to the integration, installation, and commissioning of the Inner Tracker detector. 
     This position, therefore, offers a unique opportunity to participate in the full lifecycle of a major silicon detector system, from module production and laboratory testing to detector integration and commissioning at CERN. 
 
In addition to upgrade responsibilities, the successful candidate is expected to pursue physics measurements within the CMS experiment and to contribute to the scientific activities of the Nebraska group, including mentoring graduate students and contributing to collaboration service tasks. 
 
Applicants must have a Ph.D. in experimental high energy physics or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Candidates who have received their Ph.D. within the last five years are given priority. Prior experience with silicon tracking detectors, detector instrumentation, or readout/DAQ electronics is desirable but not required. Applications must include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, publication list, and a statement of research interests.  Applicants should also arrange for at least three letters of reference to be submitted. Application materials should be sent to Jennifer Light (jlight3@unl.edu). Review of applications will begin on May 1, and will continue until the position is filled. 
 
The University of Nebraska–Lincoln is committed to building a diverse and inclusive academic community through equal opportunity, affirmative action, work-life balance initiatives, and support for dual-career families.

jobs.title: Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw Fellow Harwell
jobs.description:
BACKGROUND
The Faculty of Science and Engineering at the University of Manchester has been investing in Early Career Researchers for many years, increasing the diversity of our staff. These represent a strategic investment in outstanding researchers who will shape our future research portfolio. In 2026, we plan to appoint Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw University Research Fellowships across the Faculty. These fellowships are fixed term for 5 years and are an excellent stepping-stone to establishing an independent research career and gaining a full-time permanent academic position. We are looking for outstanding candidates who have the ability to undertake world leading in some of the following areas:

University of Manchester at Harwell
We encourage applications in areas which are aligned the University of Manchester at Harwell and our strategic partnership with the National Science Facilities based on the Harwell Campus in Oxfordshire (including, but not limited to, the Diamond Light Source, the ISIS Neutron and Muon Facility, the Central Laser Facility, Scientific Computing Division and National Quantum computing Centre), the Daresbury Laboratory (Accelerator Science and Technology Centre and cryogenic facilities, Hartree supercomputing Centre) and STFC’s Boulby Underground Laboratory (Ultra low-background science). There is particular interest in developing the areas of the use of these facilities in understanding:
  • Catalytic processes
  • Quantum materials
  • Magnetic materials
  • Formulation science and engineering.
  • Novel Detector Technologies
  • Fusion technologies
As well as the specific areas of science and engineering detailed above, the National Science Facilities and the University of Manchester have a strong desire to develop further capability in:
  • Characterisation including imaging and scattering and photoelectron emission
  • In -situ/operando environments
  • Scientific computing.
  • Novel acceleration technology
  • Low temperature science
  • Ultra low-background science
  • Applied quantum technologies.
The University actively fosters a culture of inclusion and diversity and seeks to achieve true equality of opportunity for all members of its community. The Faculty is committed to having a representative workforce. Across the Schools we hold Bronze and Silver Athena SWAN Awards, which recognise our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion and particularly the advancement of women’s education and careers in STEM.

The University also holds a Bronze Race Charter Mark recognising our commitment to improving the representation, progression and success of minority ethnic staff and students within higher education. In addition, we are a Disability Confident Employer, guaranteeing an interview for any disabled applicant who meets the minimum requirements for a job.
As an equal opportunities employer, we welcome applicants from all sections of the community regardless of age, sex, gender (or gender identity), ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation and transgender status. We strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, particularly those from underrepresented groups in academia. All appointments are made on merit. Our University is positive about flexible working – you can find out more here.

The University of Manchester
The University of Manchester (www.manchester.ac.uk) enjoys a global reputation for its research and its innovative approach to learning, with an on-going £1 billion investment in facilities, staff and buildings. This builds on our tradition of success that stretches back 200 years. The birth of the modern computer, the splitting of the atom, the founding principles of modern economics, the discovery of graphene, and the birthplace of engineering – these and many more world changing innovations have their roots at our University. We are at the forefront of the search for solutions to some of the world's most pressing problems, boasting strong collaborative links with industry and public services. In 2025, the university was second in the Times Higher Education (THE) Impact Rankings table of more than 2,500 universities globally for our impact in addressing the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw Fellowships are fully aligned with the recently launched Manchester 2035 strategy and our EDIA goals incorporating Our People, Our Values, Our Future.

APPLICATION PROCESS
Key contacts and information about the Faculty, Schools, Departments and Institutes can be found on our website (https://www.se.manchester.ac.uk/) and queries may be emailed to DKOFellows@manchester.ac.uk.
Applications should be submitted via the application form on Jobtrain together with the following supporting documents noting the maximum page numbers for each document:
  1. Curriculum Vitae (2 pages)
  2. Please also upload your Research Proposal (2 pages), Academic Impact Statement (1 page) and Statement of Strategic Fit (1 page). These three documents must be combined into a single pdf (4 pages in total)
Please ensure you indicate which Department you are applying to
Deadline for applications: 23.59 (UK time) Monday 30 March 2026.

SELECTION CRITERIA
The criteria for appointment will be based upon:
  • Overall potential of the fellowship to establish and maintain a distinctive and outstanding research and/or innovation activity
  • The quality of the proposal, particularly in relation to potential impact and deliverables
  • The relevance of the proposal to funders, industrial and/or policy stakeholders
  • Potential to act as an ambassador and advocate in their field
  • Ability to teach and communicate effectively to undergraduate and postgraduate students
SELECTION PROCESS
Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted by a panel, independently chaired by a Head of School. A shortlist of candidates will be drawn and presented to the Faculty. An interview panel chaired by the Vice President and Dean of the Faculty will carry out the final interview.
Applications are particularly welcomed from women and Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic applicants who are currently under-represented at this level. Appointments will be made on merit. We will also support requests to hold the award part-time over a proportionately longer period. Research excellence is the main criterion on which these University Research Fellowships are awarded. However, career breaks as well as unconventional research career paths will be taken into account. Evaluations will be monitored to identify potential biases, e.g. in terms of gender and race, to guarantee transparency, fairness and impartiality in the treatment of proposals.
Full details relating to eligibility; appointment details/conditions; and application procedure are outlined in the Guidance Notes that accompany this scheme.

jobs.title: Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw (DKO) University Research Fellowship - Accelerator Development With Rapiscan
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Science and Engineering (FSE) at the University of Manchester has been investing in Early Career Researchers for many years, increasing the diversity of our staff. These represent a strategic investment in outstanding researchers who will shape our future research portfolio. In 2026, we plan to appoint Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw University Research Fellowships in FSE. These fellowships are fixed term for 5 years and are an excellent stepping-stone to establishing an independent research career and gaining a full-time permanent academic position.

FSE and Rapiscan (https://www.rapiscansystems.com/en/) have for many years worked together on collaborative research in the field of security screening technologies. This has included development of x-ray CT baggage screening systems and research into novel instrumentation for x-ray cargo screening and metal detection. As a step in growing this strategic partnership we plan to appoint a Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw University Research Fellowship in a joint venture between the Faculty of Science and Engineering and Rapiscan in strategic partnership with The Cockcroft Institute (https://www.cockcroft.ac.uk). The fellowship will have a focus in accelerator development, with consideration of applications to industrial applications such as security screening. Proposals should demonstrate how they align to the industrial partner priorities in any of the following areas:

  • Development of novel RF accelerating structures to produce x-rays at the 1-10 MeV scale. This includes both high- or low-power approaches.
  • Development of high-power RF sources with a focus on compact sources for industrial applications.
  • Electron source design and dynamics, including but not limited to thermionic electron guns.
  • Development of continuous and pulsed tube-based sources in the 100-500 keV range.
  • Identification of emerging competitive accelerator or source technologies or with consideration of both performance and cost.
  • Application of AI to accelerator control and feedback systems and to accelerator design. This is expected to be a supplementary element with a primary focus on hardware system development.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Positions in Silicon Detector Development
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Research Positions in Silicon Detector Development at IHEP, Chinese Academy of Sciences
  
IHEP Introduction: 
The Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences, located in Beijing, is one of the leading research institutions in high-energy physics worldwide. With over 1,500 full-time staff and more than 900 postdoctoral researchers and graduate students, IHEP plays a central role in advancing fundamental physics and detector technologies. The institute is actively involved in major international projects and maintains strong collaborations with universities and research institutions across the globe.
  
Silicon Detector Development:
We are seeking highly motivated postdoctoral researchers to join the silicon detector group at IHEP, working on advanced silicon detector technologies for next generation high-energy physics experiments, including space-based spectrometers, future collider experiments, and medical instrument application.
 
The successful candidates will contribute to one or more of the following areas:
·  Advanced sensor development (e.g., LGAD, SiC, SDD, MAPS)
·  Front-end readout electronics and ASIC development (e.g., LGAD readout ASIC LATRIC, RISC-V SoC HERIS)
·  Sensor and ASIC testing (laser, beta source, and test-beam measurements)
·  Data acquisition (DAQ) system development
·  Detector design (e.g. beam telescopes, spectrometers)
·  Detector system integration, mechanics, and CO₂ cooling
·  Detector performance studies and data analysis
This position offers a unique and profound opportunity to work on cutting-edge detector technologies.
 
Requirements
·  Ph.D. in physics, electronics, or a related field
·  Experience in detector development, microelectronics, or data analysis
·  Strong motivation for research
 
We offer:
·  Competitive salary and benefits
·  Participation in major projects
·  Access to advanced detector and electronics facilities
·  Opportunities for international collaboration and travel
·  Good candidates after their postdoc can be promoted to tenured faculty at IHEP.
 
Application Details:
Applications should include curriculum vitae and statement of research interests.
For any questions regarding the application, please contact Professor Qi Yan at qyan@ihep.ac.cn. We look forward to your applications and to welcoming new talent to the join the silicon detector R&D.

jobs.title: PostDoc on DUNE
jobs.description:
The Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP) and Albert Einstein Center for Fundamental Physics (AEC) at the University of Bern invite applications for a

Postdoc in experimental neutrino physics

The position will be in the framework of the DUNE Experiment. The University of Bern has a long history in the development of detectors, including LArTPCs for neutrino measurement. We made major contributions to the construction, operation, and physics exploitation of experiments in Japan, Italy and the USA. A current focus is the construction of a modular, pixelated LArTPC for the DUNE near detector (ND-LAr) for which we have developed the technology in Bern. We operate a series of demonstrator setups including a four-modules setup (2x2) in the NuMI neutrino beam at Fermilab that will guide the development of the analyses of DUNE data.

The successful candidate is expected to play a leading role in the current activities of the group (e.g. light readout hardware, ND-LAr module construction, operation of prototypes, data reconstruction and analysis). Applicants must have a completed PhD in experimental high-energy physics by the start of the appointment. The net academic age (according to SNSF) is ideally less than three years and must in any case not exceed six years. Preference will be given to candidates with a background in particle physics detectors and analysis. The initial duration of the contract is for two years, extendable. The position will be located in Bern.

Candidates are requested to send a short letter of application illustrating the research interests and motivation to join our group. Also required are CV, a list of publications, and the names and e-mail addresses of three references (no need to attach letters, we will reach out after an initial selection). 

The review of applications will start April 6th, 2026 and continue until the position is filled.

Please send applications packages by email with subject “DUNE PostDoc application” to: alexandra.gerber-huisman@unibe.ch.


For further information, contact: 
Prof. Dr. Michele Weber, michele.weber@unibe.ch

jobs.title: Post-Doctoral position (2 years)
jobs.description:
Type of employment: Employment contract
Working time: Full-time
Planned duration of employment: 12 months with the possibility of extension to 24 months.
Expected date of employment commencement: July/August 2026
Deadline for submission of applications: 15.04.2026

Scope of duties:
The Candidate (F/M) will be responsible for carrying out tasks related to the analysis of experimental data collected in the HADES experiment, focusing on searches for physics beyond the Standard Model and studies of discrete symmetries, including CP symmetry in strong interactions. Additionally, the Candidate's (F/M) duties will include proposing, preparing, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations of meson production reactions and multi-pion background processes. The Candidate (F/M) will also be directly involved in future measurements and the preparation of experimental proposals using the HADES detector.
Summary of responsibilities:
  • Analysis of experimental data on rare decays of eta, omega, and eta-prime mesons.
  • Leading and conducting Monte Carlo simulations of the investigated physical processes in the context of analyzed experimental data and planned future measurements.
  • Participation in internal HADES group meetings and international conferences to present project results.
  • Collaboration with the project leader and other team members, including supervising the work of PhD students and HADES collaboration participants.
Requirements for the candidate:
The selection procedure is open for all individuals, who meet the requirements set out in Articles 113 and 116.2.3) of the Act of 20 July 2018 – Law on Higher Education and Science, and who meet the following eligibility criteria according to § 165 of the Statute of the Jagiellonian University:
  • holding at least a doctoral degree.
  • having relevant scientific achievements.
  • taking active part in scientific life.
  • Have obtained a doctoral degree no more than 7 years ago before the year of employment in the project. This period may be extended, by the principles described in the catalogue of costs in research projects financed by the National Science Centre.

  • Experience in experiments in the field of nuclear or particle physics at high or medium energy.
  • Very good knowledge and programming skills in C/C++ (or possibly Python).
  • Good knowledge of CERN-ROOT data analysis packages.
  • Knowledge of statistical data analysis methods and potential application of machine learning techniques.
  • Good command of English (B2/C1).

jobs.title: University Tenure-Track Professorship (W1) „Experimental Astroparticle Physics“
jobs.description:
We seek a candidate (f/m/d) who will expand KIT’s role in the research field of experimental astroparticle physics. The activities of the position are focused on the direct search for Dark Matter and on the development of technologies and instruments for building ultra‑sensitive experiments. The Tenure‑Track professorship will be integrated to strengthen and complement the existing experimental and theoretical activities at KIT in the research areas of astroparticle and particle physics.
You will establish and independently lead a Dark Matter research group at the KIT Institute for Astroparticle Physics (IAP). You will participate in the program‑oriented funding of the Helmholtz Association of German Research Centers, particularly in the program “Matter and the Universe” (MU). At KIT, the research topics and tasks of the program include, in addition to the search for Dark Matter, the determination of the neutrino mass and other neutrino properties as well as the investigation of ultra‑high‑energy particles and radiation from the Universe.
You will collaborate closely with colleagues from other institutes and the program “Matter and Technologies” (MT), especially for the development of suitable detection technologies and detectors. You contribute in the acquisition of third‑party funding from national and international sources.
A participation in the KIT Center for Elementary Particle and Astroparticle Physics (KCETA) and in the Karlsruhe School for Elementary Particle and Astroparticle Physics: Science and Technology (KSETA) is desired.
An appropriate participation in the teaching duties of the KIT Faculty of Physics is expected. You will perform large-scale research with a teaching load of 4 lecture hours per week per semester and after a positive mid-term evaluation of 6 lecture hours per week per semester.

Personal qualification
Desired for a successful application is a competitively acquired junior research group (e.g. German Research Foundation (DFG) Emmy Noether Young Investigators Group, Helmholtz Young Investigator Groups, ERC Starting Grant, junior research groups of German ministries (esp. the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, BMFTR)), with less than half of the funding period expired at the time of publication of this advertisement.
Prerequisites are a completed doctorate in physics, outstanding internationally visible scientific achievements in the field of experimental astroparticle physics and suitable pedagogical skills.
Employment is subject to Art. 14, par. (2) of the KIT Act in conjunction with Art. 47 LHG Baden-Württemberg (Act of Baden-Württemberg on Universities and Colleges) and the Quality Assurance Concept for Junior Professorships and Tenure-track Professorships at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology.

As a family-friendly university, KIT offers part-time employment, leaves of absence, a dual career service, and coaching to support the work-life balance. We prefer to balance the number of employees (f/m/d). Therefore, we encourage female applicants to apply for this job.

Recognized severely disabled persons will be preferred if they are equally qualified.

jobs.title: Postdoc (ATLAS/FCCee)
jobs.description:
The Particle Physics Department (DPNC) of the University of Geneva invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in collider physics, with a focus on the ATLAS experiment at CERN’s LHC and preparations for the FCC-ee. 

The DPNC plays a key role in collider physics, contributing to the ATLAS and FASER experiments at CERN’s LHC. It has made significant contributions to detector construction and operation, particularly in tracking and TDAQ systems. The department is now expanding its involvement in FCC-ee activities.

The successful candidate will work with Prof. Anna Sfyrla and Prof. Steven Schramm at the University of Geneva. Research directions will be defined flexibly according to the candidate’s interests, along the following lines:
  • ATLAS: Phase II TDAQ upgrade (Level 0, algorithms) and searches for new physics (hadronic final states)
  • FCC-ee: TDAQ development, computing and searches for FIPs / LLPs
Qualifications
We seek an outstanding and highly motivated physicist who has completed, or is close to completing, a PhD in experimental particle physics. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
  • A record of independent, high-quality research.
  • Experience with data analysis in a collider experiment.
  • Strong ability to collaborate within an international team.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills.
  • Experience with electronics, trigger and data acquisition systems, or machine learning (an asset).
In addition to research, the candidate will contribute to student supervision and teaching within the Physics Section at the University of Geneva.

Terms of appointment
  • The position is renewable annually for up to three years.
  • Preference will be given to candidates with fewer than three years of postdoctoral experience, though applications from more experienced researchers are welcome.
  • Professional development opportunities include workshops, conferences, and collaborative research projects.
Application procedure
  • Inquiries: Prof. Anna Sfyrla (anna.sfyrla_at_cern.ch) and/or Prof. Steven Schramm (steven.schramm_at_cern.ch).
  • Applications: submit via this form.
  • Review of applications will start immediately as they are received and will continue until the position is filled. For full consideration, applications should be submitted by 11 April 2026.
  • The position is available starting in September 2026.
  • NB: No need to provide reference letters yet. You will be contacted to provide those after an initial review of applications.
Commitment to diversity
The University of Geneva is committed to fostering diversity and inclusion. We strongly encourage applications from underrepresented groups in the scientific community.
Contact: Sfyrla, Anna (anna.sfyrla@cern.ch); Schramm, Steven Randolph (steven.schramm@cern.ch)

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate -- CMS Experiment
jobs.description:
The experimental particle physics group at Northeastern University invites applications for a postdoctoral research associate position on the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment. The position is available immediately, with a preferred start date in Spring or Summer 2026, and will be primarily based at CERN.

The Northeastern CMS group is active in many aspects of the experiment, including physics data analysis, detector operations, and HL-LHC detector upgrades (group website: https://epp.sites.northeastern.edu). Current physics efforts include measurements and searches in the top quark and Higgs boson sectors, as well as searches for exotic long-lived particles.

The successful candidate is expected to take a leading role in CMS physics analysis and to contribute significantly to the CMS Track Trigger development for the HL-LHC upgrade. The candidate will also have opportunities to work closely with graduate and undergraduate students.

Applicants should send (1) a CV, including a publication list; (2) a research statement describing past experience and future interests; and (3) should arrange for at least three letters of recommendation to be sent directly to Prof. Louise Skinnari at l.skinnari@northeastern.edu. 

Review of applications will begin immediately. For full consideration, applications should be received by April 15, 2026, but the position will remain open until filled.

A Ph.D. in experimental particle physics by the time of the appointment is required. Candidates should have a strong record of recent accomplishments in physics data analysis and detector hardware and/or software. The appointment is nominally for one year, with the possibility of renewal for up to five years total, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.

jobs.title: Senior Assistant in Experimental Particle Physics - CMS (ECAL)
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Science, University of Split (PMF), announces an open call for applications for one position of Senior Assistant in the scientific area of Natural Sciences, field of Physics, to work on the Croatian Science Foundation project “Integration, Testing and Optimization of a Homogeneous Electromagnetic Calorimeter.”

The position is fixed-term and will last until 30 November 2027.

The selected candidate will contribute to the development, testing, and integration of the Data Acquisition (DAQ) and Data Quality Monitor (DQM) software modules, as well as to the upgrade of the ECAL barrel front-end electronics, in accordance with the project objectives.

The candidate will be expected to:
  • develop and maintain the preliminary version of the Data Acquisition (DAQ) and Data Quality Monitor (DQM) software modules, and present progress and results at collaboration meetings;
  • test the DAQ and DQM software modules on a single trigger tower using new front-end electronics;
  • participate in the replacement of the ECAL barrel front-end electronics and document the process.

Additional requirements:
  • experience in data analysis in the field of high-energy physics
  • very good knowledge of the programming languages Python and C++, especially in the context of hardware control and management

Preference will be given to candidates with:
  • experience in developing, installing, and testing hardware in the field of high-energy physics
  • experience working with Kubernetes and SQL tools

Applicants should have good written and oral communication skills in English.

Applicants must meet the general requirements prescribed by the Higher Education and Scientific Activity Act (OG 119/22).

Applicants must submit the following documents with their signed application: a curriculum vitae, a copy of the diploma confirming completion of the relevant study programme, a decision or opinion on the recognition of a foreign higher education qualification (for applicants who obtained their qualification abroad), a certified transcript of grades from undergraduate and graduate or integrated studies including the calculated grade average, and proof of citizenship.

Applicants who invoke the right to priority in employment in accordance with special regulations are required to invoke this right in their application for the competition and have priority over other candidates only under equal conditions set out in the competition, and on the basis of a proper, complete and timely application for the competition. Applicants who invoke the right to priority in employment in accordance with Articles 102 and 103 of the Act on Croatian Homeland War Veterans and Members of Their Families (Official Gazette No. 121/17, 98/19, 84/21, 156/23) are required to submit, in addition to evidence of meeting the required conditions, all necessary evidence from Article 103, paragraph 1, available at the link of the Ministry of Croatian Veterans https://branitelji.gov.hr/zaposljavanje-843/843.

By submitting an application for the competition, applicants expressly agree that the PMF, as the controller of the personal data collection, may collect, use, and further process their personal data for the purpose of conducting the competition procedure, in accordance with the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Act.

For applicants who meet the formal requirements of the competition, a test of knowledge and abilities relevant to the duties of the position may be conducted, through testing and/or interviews. All information regarding the test will be published on the official website of the PMF (https://www.pmfst.unist.hr) at least five days before the test. If an applicant does not attend the test, it will be considered that the applicant has withdrawn their application. Applicants will be notified of the date, time, and place of the test by email sent to the address provided in their application.

Applicants of both sexes are equally eligible to apply.

Applications must be submitted within 30 days of the publication of the call for applications in the Official Gazette to the email address natjecaj-posao@pmfst.hr.

A complete application is considered to be one that contains all required attachments and is signed by hand. Late or incomplete applications will not be considered, and applicants with incomplete applications will not be invited to supplement their applications.

Applicants will be notified of the results of the call for applications within the legally prescribed deadline.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Position in Experimental Particle Physics
jobs.description:
The Collaborative Innovation Center for Particles and Interactions (CICPI) at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the LHCb experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. The particle physics laboratory at USTC is a leading research center in China. USTC is currently a Technical Associate of the LHCb collaboration and is applying for full or associate membership. The USTC LHCb group has a strong focus on LHCb physics analyses and on the MUON detector project for the LHCb Phase-2 Upgrade.

Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in experimental particle physics, or expect to receive one soon. Candidates should have excellent data analysis skills and/or solid experience in particle detector instrumentation, as well as the ability to conduct independent research. The successful candidate is expected to play a key role in LHCb physics analyses and will also have opportunities to contribute to the MUON detector project for the LHCb Phase-2 Upgrade.
The initial appointment will be for two years, with the possibility of extension. The salary will be competitive and commensurate with the experience of the selected candidate. The successful applicant may be based at CERN or at USTC, subject to mutual agreement.

Applications should be submitted by April 30, 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position will remain open until filled. Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae (including a list of publications), a statement of research interests, and arrange for three letters of reference to be sent by the referees via email to Prof. Zehua Xu (zehua.xu@ustc.edu.cn).

Inquiries about the position are welcome and should be sent to the same email address.

The successful candidate is expected to take a leading role in physics analyses of the

The successful candidate will work as part of the CBM Collaboration (https://www.cbm.gsi.de/) and project oriented on studies of the feasibility study of D mesons and Lambda_c hyperon production and semi-leptonic hyperon (Lambda, Xi) decays in p+p collisions in the energy range of 4.5-30 GeV, using the CBMRoot package. The successful candidate will also focus on the investigation of possible background sources using transport codes (GiBUU, SMASH) and the PLUTO event generator.

  • scientific achievements documented by publications in prestigious international scientific journals,
  • knowledge of the research topics and current activity in the field of nuclear physics or elementary particles at intermediate energies,
  • experience in experimental data analysis and simulations,
  • good knowledge of the ROOT package,
  • good programming skills in C/C++/Python, ability to create own programming tools and to integrate them with existing software written in C++ in Linux environment,

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • active participation in weekly discussions and in working meetings (at least every few weeks), and presenting results on these meetings,
  • dissemination of the research results in the form of publications in leading scientific journals indexed in the JCR and speeches during seminars and conferences, including international ones,
  • applying for external funding for research.

jobs.title: Two postdoctoral Research Associate positions on the ATLAS experiment with the ERC DITTO project
jobs.description:
The CNRS LAPP (Laboratoire d'Annecy de Physique des Particules) institute is opening two post-doctoral research associate positions to work on the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN. The work is funded through the ERC Consolidator Grant DITTO (2023-2029).

The goal of the DITTO project is to provide the complete set of differential cross-section measurements for dilepton production (Drell-Yan scattering) covering not only the light lepton channels ev/μv/ee/µµ, but also extremely challenging third generation τv and ττ final states. These high mass Drell-Yan scattering measurements (HMDY) will be used to probe new phenomena at mass scales beyond the reach of direct production at the LHC through the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework.

The successful candidates are expected to take the leading role in the ATLAS HMDY measurements based on the combined LHC Run 2 (2015-2018) and Run 3 (2022-2025) data sets.

They will be also expected to contribute to the electron or tau-lepton performance studies with the goal to ensure the best possible precision of the dilepton production measurements at high mass. In particular, the DITTO team works with computing scientists from the Laboratory of Computer Science, Systems, Information and Knowledge Processing (LISTIC) of the Savoie Mont Blanc University in Annecy on development of innovative algorithms for the ATLAS electron identification algorithms for the HL-LHC data-taking (2030+) in both real-time (trigger) and offline physics analysis environments applying the cutting-edge machine-learning techniques.

Postdoctoral research associate candidates should hold a Ph.D. degree in particle physics. A strong experience in analyses of LHC data based on C/C++ and Python, knowledge of statistical techniques for data analysis for high energy physics experiments, software development including deep learning techniques and knowledge of PyTorch or TensorFlow frameworks is required. More details on the position and skills requirements can be found at https://emploi.cnrs.fr/Offres/CDD/UMR5814-LOUDAI-051/Default.aspx?lang=EN

Applicants must apply on the CNRS Job Portal:
  • submit a cover letter explaining their interest in the position and a detailed curriculum vitae (containing a description of their research experience with a list of publications highlighting their personal contributions);
  • have their referees send at least two letters of recommendation directly to contact.rh@lapp.in2p3.fr.
Selection will be carried out starting from 1st of April 2026 until the positions are filled. The positions are expected to start on 1st of September 2026.

The positions will be initially for a period of two years with a possibility of an extension. They is based at LAPP, with the possibility to travel to CERN regularly (50 km from LAPP). Supervision of student internships is foreseen (undergraduate and Master level).

Further information on the positions can be obtained by sending e-mail to contact.rh@lapp.in2p3.fr.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral position in the neutrino physics and direct dark matter detection
jobs.description:
The Neutrino and Dark Matter direct detection group at University of Hawaii has an opening for a postdoctoral research associate position. Qualified candidates are invited to apply.
 
The group is involved in DUNE and KamLAND-Zen neutrino experiments and the DarkSide-20k direct dark matter detection experiment. The group’s experimental focus is on the calibration of charge and light in liquid argon TPCs and the calibration of liquid scintillator detectors, physics analysis and simulations. We are looking for outstanding postdoctoral candidates to join us in the pursuit of new physics and building state-of-the-art detectors. The successful applicants will have an opportunity to work on two projects of their choice out of the three listed projects. The group members enjoy a stimulating research environment within the Hawaii High Energy Physics Group that spans high-energy theory, B-physics, cosmic rays, astrophysics and instrumentation.
 
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. degree in experimental particle physics or a closely related field. The successful candidates will enjoy significant freedom in choosing their research topic, and will be expected to actively participate in hardware and simulation activities that the group is involved in. If you are interested in joining the neutrino and dark matter group at the University of Hawaii, please send your application package to the following email maricic@hawaii.edu with the subject line Postdoctoral application – ‘name’. The application should include a cover letter, CV, research statement (include previous experience, and future plans, with 2 pages maximum length), and arrange for at least three letters of reference to be sent.
 
Any inquiries on the position can be sent to Prof. Jelena Maricic (maricic@hawaii.edu). The initial application is March 31, 2026. However, late applications will be accepted and considered until the positions are filled. The start date of the position as soon as the candidate as available to join the group.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral research associate
jobs.description:
The Instituto Galego de Física de Altas Enerxías (IGFAE) seeks applications for a post-doctoral researcher position dedicated to the CMS experiment. IGFAE is a joint research institute of the University of Santiago de Compostela and the regional government of Galicia. Recognized as a "María de Maeztu" Unit of Excellence, IGFAE offers a highly dynamic and international research environment with a strong track record and prominent participation in major particle, astroparticle, and nuclear physics experiments.

We are currently establishing a newly formed CMS group at IGFAE, and the successful candidate will play a foundational role in building and shaping this team. We are searching for exceptional candidates at the postdoctoral level with a strong background in Experimental Particle Physics. Given the foundational nature of this position, previous experience within the CMS collaboration is highly desirable, as the candidate is expected to provide supervision, mentorship, and general guidance to the junior members of the new group.

The successful candidate is expected to drive a strong physics analysis program, with a primary focus on searches for dark sectors and Long-Lived Particles. In addition to data analysis, the candidate will actively contribute to key technical activities critical for the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade. Specifically, they will be expected to contribute to Run 4 trigger development as well as detector software development, namely for the MIP Timing Detector.

We offer an initial appointment of two years, which can be extended depending on mutual satisfaction and funding availability. The candidate must have their PhD in Physics or a related field concluded by the start of the contract. The anticipated start date is around September 2026, although earlier starting dates could be accommodated upon mutual agreement.

Interested candidates should submit their applications along with a curriculum vitae, a statement of research interests, and two letters of recommendation via email to xabier.cid.vidal@cern.ch (the letters might be sent directly by the referees).
For any inquiries regarding the position or the application process, please contact Xabier Cid Vidal at the same email address (xabier.cid.vidal@cern.ch).

jobs.title: CMS Postdoctoral Researcher Position
jobs.description:
The University of Cyprus (UCY) experimental particle physics group [1] has one available position for a Special Research Scientist to work on the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC.

The UCY, founded in 1989, is in the top 100 Young Universities of the Times Higher Education ranking. The Department of Physics, based in Nicosia, consists of academics working on various research areas including both experimental and theoretical particle physics. The UCY CMS group consists of two faculty members, three postdoctoral researchers/special research scientists, and six graduate students, with major involvements in physics analyses as well as hadron calorimeter and trigger software operations, and upgrades.

The group is currently leading multiple analyses for BSM physics in a variety of leptonic and hadronic final states and event topologies. The advertised position will be funded by The Research and Innovation Foundation [1] Programmes for Research, Technological Development and Innovation "Restart 2016 – 2020" in Cyprus, under the «Excellence Hubs» program proposal number Excellence/0524/0469.

Applicants need not be citizens of the Republic of Cyprus. Applicants should however ensure, before applying, that in case they are selected they will be residing in Cyprus on a full-time basis during the employment period; submission of application implies acceptance of this condition.

Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in experimental high-energy physics or a related field by appointment start date, and possess strong data analysis and software development skills. Experience with student mentoring and MC simulation tools will be considered an asset.

Applications will be reviewed as soon as they are completed, and successful applicants will be invited for an online interview.

For all enquiries about the position, please contact Prof. Halil Saka (saka.halil@ucy.ac.cy).

jobs.title: PhD Position in Experimental Particle and Nuclear Physics (STAR / ePIC)
jobs.description:
The Czech Technical University in Prague invites applications for a PhD position in experimental particle and nuclear physics at the Faculty of Nuclear Sciences and Physical Engineering (FNSPE). The expected start date is 1 October 2026.
The position is funded by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic through the projects INTER-ACTION MSMT-355/2025-9 “Study of hard probes in proton and nucleus collisions” and LM2023034 Brookhaven National Laboratory – Participation of the Czech Republic. 

Location
The position will be based at FNSPE CTU in Prague, Czech Republic, and includes opportunities for conference travel and short research stays at collaborating institutions.

Research Environment and Supervision
The successful candidate will join the RHIC–STAR / EIC–ePIC group at CTU Prague and work within the international STAR Experiment and ePIC Experiment collaborations at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) and the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory (New York, USA) under the supervision of Dr. Barbara Trzeciak and Doc. Mgr. Jaroslav Bielčík, Ph.D.

Description
The project focuses on studying quarkonia production in high-energy collisions using recent large datasets collected by the STAR experiment at RHIC. These measurements aim to shed new light on the still poorly understood mechanisms of quarkonium production. The research will also include feasibility studies of quarkonium measurements with the ePIC experiment at the future EIC, providing an important connection between current and future experimental facilities.

Responsibilities
The PhD student will:
  • Participation in the scientific activities of the CTU STAR/ePIC group
  • Perform physics analysis of data from the STAR experiment at RHIC, with a focus on quarkonium measurements
  • Contribute to feasibility studies of quarkonium production measurements with the ePIC experiment
  • Fulfillment of scientific research and educational activity plans
  • Present research results at national and international conferences
  • Publish results in peer-reviewed scientific journals
  • Participate in seminars, workshops, and collaboration meetings
  • Contribute to knowledge transfer within the group (e.g. seminars or tutorials)
Required Qualifications
Applicants should have:
  • Completed M. Sc degree program in a European University, a foreign equivalent University recognised in the Czech Republic by Act No. 111/1998 Coll., on Higher Education Institutions and on Amendments and Supplements to some other Acts (The Higher Education Act)
  • Experience in scientific research within a professional research team, preferably in the field of experimental particle or nuclear physics
  • Proficiency in English, both written and spoken
  • Working knowledge of a modern programming language (e.g., C++, Python);
  • Creative approach to solving work tasks
  • Strong motivation for research and the ability to work both independently and within an international collaboration
Contract and Financial Conditions
  • Full-time fixed-term contract: October 2026 – June 2030
  • Gross salary: 25,500 CZK/month
  • PhD scholarship: 13,000 CZK/month (net)
  • Six weeks of paid vacation per year
  • Travel support for conferences, workshops, and collaboration meetings

Application
Applicants should send the following documents by email to Dr. Barbara Trzeciak and Doc. Mgr. Jaroslav Bielčík, Ph.D.
  • Curriculum Vitae
  • Brief statement of research interests
  • Copy of a M. Sc degree diploma or certificates of studies, or its foreign equivalent with a translation; candidates must complete all M. Sc degree requirements before starting their appointment
  • List of courses completed during previous studies
  • Two reference letters
  • List of publications (if any)
  • List of conference or workshop presentations (if any)
The application and all the annexes listed above must be signed by the applicant.

Application Deadline
10 April 2026 at 24:00 CET

Interviews will take place in late April 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to prepare a 15-minute presentation summarizing their background and research experience, followed by a discussion with the selection committee on topics related to experimental nuclear and particle physics.

The selected candidate must also complete the official admission procedure to the Doctoral School at FNSPE CTU, in the study field: Nuclear Engineering, specialisation Experimental Nuclear and Particle Physics. 
The Doctoral School program starts on 1 October 2026, with an official application deadline of 21 May 2026. Further information:
https://www.fjfi.cvut.cz/en/education/doctoral-study/admission-procedure

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Position in Experimental Particle Physics - LHCb
jobs.description:
The Collaborative Innovation Center for Particles and Interactions (CICPI) at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the LHCb experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. The particle physics laboratory at USTC is a leading research center in China. USTC is currently a Technical Associate of the LHCb collaboration and is applying for full or associate membership. The USTC LHCb group has a strong focus on LHCb physics analyses and on the MUON detector project for the LHCb Phase-2 Upgrade.

Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in experimental particle physics, or expect to receive one soon. Candidates should have excellent data analysis skills and/or solid experience in particle detector instrumentation, as well as the ability to conduct independent research. The successful candidate is expected to play a key role in LHCb physics analyses and will also have opportunities to contribute to the MUON detector project for the LHCb Phase-2 Upgrade.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
jobs.description:
The experimental particle physics group working in LHCb is soliciting applications for a position of Postdoctoral Research Associate to work in the LHCb experiment at LHC, and its upgrades.

The Syracuse team is involved in physics analysis, software tasks associated with the optimization of the performance of the Upstream Tracker (UT) detector, and major R&D initiatives to optimize the technology choices of major LHCb Upgrade II detector components. There are several cutting-edge projects related to the sensor and electronics infrastructure needed for a novel tracking detector, the Upstream Pixel (UP) detector for Upgrade II, based on the HV-MAP technology. We are working towards several key system-level R&D efforts, such as key aspects of the detector mechanics, optimization of powering schemes and data transmission, and investigation of heterogeneous computing involving FPGAs and GPUs. This work relates to our commitment to develop innovative detectors that will meet the challenging basic research needs of future experiments. We are members of the DRD3 collaboration, play a leading role in the CPAD-RDC9 R&D stream and are interested in developing innovative particle identification detectors for future high-luminosity colliders. In addition, we are pursuing several exciting physics analysis projects, ranging from conventional and exotic spectroscopy to precision Standard Model tests and searches for new physics, exploiting the unique opportunities offered by b-quark decays. 

The initial appointment is for one year, renewable up to three years. The successful applicant can be stationed either at Syracuse University or CERN. While the primary responsibility will be the work on the UP detector, we encourage the successful candidate to pursue physics analysis projects in collaboration with one of the Syracuse faculty.

The position is currently open, and we will accept applications until the job is filled. Interested applicant can submit their application packet, that should include highlights of research achievements and a research goals statement, at: https://www.sujobopps.com/postings/102607

jobs.title: PhD student position in experimental particle physics (LHCb experiment)
jobs.description:
The High Energy Physics Laboratory [1] of EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, invites applications for a PhD student position in experimental particle physics. The successful candidate will join the LHCb collaboration in which the lab is strongly involved. LHCb [2] is a particle-physics experiment running at CERN's Large Hadron Collider and dedicated to flavour physics.

The lab’s LHCb activities have been expanded through an SNSF-funded programme focused on charm physics very recently. The successful candidate will join this programme, and contribute to measurements using the data of the upgraded LHCb detector, closely collaborating in a team of another PhD student, two postdocs and the PI. The candidate will focus on measurements of properties of charm hadrons, with a focus on CP violation in challenging decays involving pi0 mesons. This work includes the study of experimental biases in the reconstruction of charged particles and the development of techniques that can be applied in Run 4 of the LHC, when the experiment’s PID detectors have been upgraded. There is also an option to engage in studies related to the event reconstruction for upgrades of the LHCb experiment in the far future (Run 5 and beyond).

The position, which also involves teaching responsibilities at the bachelor’s or master’s level, becomes available on September 1st, 2026. A delayed start is possible, but not later than October 1st, 2026. Once selected, the PhD student will need to enrol in the Physics program (EDPY) of the EPFL doctoral school [3]. The employment runs up to a total of four years. Doctoral school information and employment conditions at EPFL may be consulted online [3-5]. Applicants are expected to hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in physics at the start of employment. The candidate should have a strong motivation for fundamental research, and received education in Particle Physics. Experience with data analysis, computer programming and/or track reconstruction is an advantage, especially in the context of high-energy particle physics.

Applicants should prepare:
  • a motivation letter;
  • their CV;
  • scans of the higher-institution grade records;
  • contact information of at least two references willing to write a recommendation. Providing one additional reference is possible, but optional. 
Please note that the letters of recommendation should be submitted by the references within 7 days following the deadline of the application.

The application should be submitted online at

by the deadline of April 30th, 2026.

jobs.title: Doctoral student for the development and construction of the pixel detector at the INSIGHT experiment
jobs.description:
The Cluster of Excellence “Color meets Flavor” has an opening for

a doctoral student in experimental particle physics for the development and construction of the INSIGHT experiment

The Cluster aims to explain the interaction of weak and strong interactions at different energy scales in order to answer fundamental questions about the structure of matter. It is a collaboration of the Universities in Bonn, Dortmund, and Siegen, as well as the Forschungszentrum Jülich.

One of the central experiments for studying strong interactions at the energy scale of light quarks is the planned INSIGHT photo-production experiment at the ELSA electron accelerator in Bonn. We are involved in the construction of the pixel detector for the experiment and are looking for a doctoral student for the development and construction of the
detector. Your tasks will include the optimization of the detector design based on simulations, the assembly and testing of pixel modules, and the integration and commissioning of the pixel detector.

Excellent applicants are encouraged to apply. They should hold (or are about to complete) a master's degree in physics or a closely related field. Relevant experience in detector development will be an advantage. The position is located at Siegen, a cozy, international University town, with the possibility of frequent travels to Bonn and/or a stay of several months. An attractive salary is offered.

The position is available immediately for an appointment of three years. Applications will be reviewed in the order they are received. The University of Siegen is an equal-opportunity employer. To apply, please prepare the following material and send it by e-mail to markus.cristinziani@uni-siegen.de before March 31st, 2026, to receive full consideration:

  •     If English or German is not your first language, we would also like to have proof of your English language ability. Please include your certificate with your application if you have already taken an English language qualification. We will also consider your application without this document.

jobs.title: POSTDOCTORAL POSITION IN CMS
jobs.description:
The experimental Particle Physics Departement of the Université Libre de Bruxelles - ULB invites applications for a 3-year postdoctoral research position within the CMS collaboration at the LHC.
 
The Department is part of the Inter-University Institute for High Energies IIHE (ULB-VUB), which combines the experimental particle and astroparticle research groups from both Brussels universities, ULB and VUB, and presently numbers more than 100 physicists, engineers and support persons. It is involved in large international collaborations: CMS (at the LHC) and JUNO (in China), IceCube (at the South Pole), RNO-G (in Greenland) and Auger (in Argentina). It has R&D activities in detector development and readout systems. It hosts a CMS Grid Tier-2 computing center.
 
The CMS ULB group counts about 35 active members. It is involved in several data analyses, among which the study of electroweak symmetry breaking, searches for physics beyond the Standard Model, precision measurements of electroweak processes and of jet production, search for dark matter signatures, some of them using Machine Learning techniques. The group is contributing e.g. to jet calibration, trigger developments and central tracker data quality monitoring. The team is participating to the CMS detector upgrades – in the design and tests of the muon detectors and their readout in the forward regions, as well as in the design and construction of the central tracker for the LHC Phase 2. In particular, the IIHE hosts one of the assembly sites for CMS Outer Tracker Silicon strip modules, so-called “2S” (strip-strip) modules. We are committed to build and fully test 1600 such modules by end 2027. We are also contributing to tests of new Silicon sensors.

The successful candidate will lead activities in the construction and commissioning of the CMS Outer Tracker upgrade. Until the end of the production in Brussels, the candidate is expected to contribute to the quality assurance of the modules. In parallel, as well as after the production, the candidate will contribute to the commissioning of the outer tracker, by integrating the experience gained during the module construction and tests into the tracker detailed simulation, by developing signal reconstruction, data quality monitoring and procedures to commission the tracker, using real and simulated cosmic muons, and with simulated proton collision events. The position implies frequent visits to CERN. The salary is competitive and includes all social security benefits (information is available on request). Contributions to teaching are possible but are not mandatory. The candidate should be in the condition of international mobility (the researcher should not have resided or carried out his/her main activity (contract, studies...) in Belgium for more than 24 months during the 3 years directly preceding the beginning of the present postdoctoral fellowship.

The position is open until filled, and the contract would start on October 1st, 2026. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply before March 31st, 2026. Applications should be sent by email (with subject “CMS – post-doc position”) to Prof. Pascal Vanlaer. They should include a detailed CV, a transcript of grades of Master studies, a copy of the PhD diploma if already available, a letter of motivation and the names of 3 referees.
 
Contact : Prof. Pascal Vanlaer : Pascal.Vanlaer@ulb.be
Phone :  +32-2-629.3898
IIHE web site : http://w3.iihe.ac.be
